missing_patients.note_en: 54 new patients a year x (27% nationally - 28.3% here) = 0 patients a year (0-2.2 from the exact 95% interval of the county's share; floored at 0). Against the share reached by the best quarter of counties (30.4%) it is 1.1 a year. Arithmetic on registry shares, not a causal estimate: counties differ in age, stage at diagnosis and other illness, and the registry cannot say which of these patients could have been treated to cure.

headroom.note_en: Patients a year between this county's curative share and the share of the best quarter of counties.

expected.method_en: Expected share = what a county with this share of residents aged 65 or over would have if it followed the pattern of the other 21 counties (quasi-binomial regression of curative-intent counts on the county's 65+ share, fitted without the county itself). Ratio = observed / expected; the interval allows for counties varying 4.1 times more than chance alone. This is an ecological adjustment: it uses the age of the county's residents, not of its patients, because the registry publishes neither the national share by age nor the age of each county's patients. It can remove an age-structure difference between counties; it cannot show why a county differs.
adjusted_for: share of county residents aged 65 or over (Statistics Finland, county level)
not_adjusted_for: stage at diagnosis (unknown for 48% of patients nationally, so it cannot be used)
how the cancer was found (symptoms, incidental, emergency)
treatment given outside the county's own records
expected.distance_en: Distance to the university hospital is reported, not adjusted away, because distance is part of access to treatment. Across counties the curative share falls with distance (Spearman rho -0.66, permutation p 0.000); after the 65+ adjustment the link is rho -0.30 (p 0.18). Distance and age structure go together in Finland, so 22 counties cannot separate them.
expected.why_not_standardised_en: Indirect standardisation by age and stage was not possible: the registry's public report gives the curative share for all patients only, not by age group or stage, and stage is unknown for 48% of patients.

by_modality.note_en: 90 patients a year x (national operated share 14.9% - this county's 12.2%), capped at the total. Operated shares are the registry's age-standardised 6-month figures for 2018-mid 2022 (mean of men and women), a different period than the total.

The rest: total minus the surgery part. missing_patients.split_method_en: Surgery part from the county's operated share against the national one; the remainder is assigned to curative radiotherapy by subtraction.
missing_patients.note_en: 90 new patients a year x (27% nationally - 23.4% here) = 3.2 patients a year (0-6.6 from the exact 95% interval of the county's share). Against the share reached by the best quarter of counties (30.4%) it is 6.2 a year. headroom.note_en: Patients a year between this county's curative share and the share of the best quarter of counties.

expected.method_en: Expected share = what a county with this share of residents aged 65 or over would have if it followed the pattern of the other 21 counties (quasi-binomial regression of curative-intent counts on the county's 65+ share, fitted without the county itself). Ratio = observed / expected; the interval allows for counties varying 4.1 times more than chance alone. This is an ecological adjustment: it uses the age of the county's residents, not of its patients, because the registry publishes neither the national share by age nor the age of each county's patients. It can remove an age-structure difference between counties; it cannot show why a county differs.

missing_patients.note_en: 90 new patients a year x (27% nationally - 27.8% here) = 0 patients a year (0-3 from the exact 95% interval of the county's share; floored at 0). Against the share reached by the best quarter of counties (30.4%) it is 2.3 a year. Arithmetic on registry shares, not a causal estimate: counties differ in age, stage at diagnosis and other illness, and the registry cannot say which of these patients could have been treated to cure.

headroom.note_en: Patients a year between this county's curative share and the share of the best quarter of counties.

expected.method_en: Expected share = what a county with this share of residents aged 65 or over would have if it followed the pattern of the other 21 counties (quasi-binomial regression of curative-intent counts on the county's 65+ share, fitted without the county itself). Ratio = observed / expected; the interval allows for counties varying 4.1 times more than chance alone. This is an ecological adjustment: it uses the age of the county's residents, not of its patients, because the registry publishes neither the national share by age nor the age of each county's patients. It can remove an age-structure difference between counties; it cannot show why a county differs.
adjusted_for: share of county residents aged 65 or over (Statistics Finland, county level)
not_adjusted_for: stage at diagnosis (unknown for 48% of patients nationally, so it cannot be used)
how the cancer was found (symptoms, incidental, emergency)
treatment given outside the county's own records
expected.distance_en: Distance to the university hospital is reported, not adjusted away, because distance is part of access to treatment. Across counties the curative share falls with distance (Spearman rho -0.66, permutation p 0.000); after the 65+ adjustment the link is rho -0.30 (p 0.18). Distance and age structure go together in Finland, so 22 counties cannot separate them.
expected.why_not_standardised_en: Indirect standardisation by age and stage was not possible: the registry's public report gives the curative share for all patients only, not by age group or stage, and stage is unknown for 48% of patients.

registry_age_standardised_surgery.note_en: The registry's own adjustment, for surgery only: operated share standardised to the age of all Finnish patients (four age groups), by sex, with its 95% confidence interval. Where the interval lies below the national share, age does not explain the county's lower operated share.

expected.sentence_en: Observed 27.8%, expected 27.6% for a county with 23.7% of residents aged 65+: ratio 1.01 (0.73-1.39). Within the range the county's age structure predicts.

stages.note_en: Age-standardised share alive 12 months after diagnosis; published by sex, the value is the mean of men and women. Survival follows stage at diagnosis and age as well as treatment.

expected.method_en: Expected share = what a county with this share of residents aged 65 or over would have if it followed the pattern of the other 21 counties (quasi-binomial regression of curative-intent counts on the county's 65+ share, fitted without the county itself). Ratio = observed / expected; the interval allows for counties varying 4.1 times more than chance alone. This is an ecological adjustment: it uses the age of the county's residents, not of its patients, because the registry publishes neither the national share by age nor the age of each county's patients. It can remove an age-structure difference between counties; it cannot show why a county differs.
adjusted_for: share of county residents aged 65 or over (Statistics Finland, county level)
not_adjusted_for: stage at diagnosis (unknown for 48% of patients nationally, so it cannot be used)
how the cancer was found (symptoms, incidental, emergency)
treatment given outside the county's own records
expected.distance_en: Distance to the university hospital is reported, not adjusted away, because distance is part of access to treatment. Across counties the curative share falls with distance (Spearman rho -0.66, permutation p 0.000); after the 65+ adjustment the link is rho -0.30 (p 0.18). Distance and age structure go together in Finland, so 22 counties cannot separate them.
expected.why_not_standardised_en: Indirect standardisation by age and stage was not possible: the registry's public report gives the curative share for all patients only, not by age group or stage, and stage is unknown for 48% of patients.

main_leak.sentence_en: Of 100 lung cancer patients in Finland, 27 get treatment that aims to cure. By county it runs from 18 in Lapland to 36 in Vantaa and Kerava. Bringing every county below the national share up to it is about 66 patients a year; 50 of them are in the 7 counties that are below it by more than chance.
main_leak.sentence_fi: Suomessa sadasta keuhkosyöpäpotilaasta 27 saa parantavaan pyrkivää hoitoa. Alueittain luku vaihtelee 18:stä 36:een. Jos jokainen maan keskiarvon alle jäävä alue nousisi keskiarvoon, se tarkoittaisi noin 66 potilasta vuodessa. Heistä 50 on niillä 7 alueella, jotka jäävät keskiarvosta satunnaisvaihtelua enemmän.

missing_patients.note_en: Sum over counties of patients a year x (national share - county share), counties above the national share counted as 0: 66 a year. Against the best quarter of counties (30.4%): 123 a year. 7 of 22 counties are below the national share beyond chance; they account for 50 of the 66. Arithmetic, not a causal estimate.
